method: Explicit direct control-to-technique pilot candidates. Each row is independently selected from discovery evidence and remains non-public until an exact human review decision is recorded.

unmapped.reason: No technique-specific direct candidate met the evidence threshold for this initial pilot; discovery relationships remain available for later review.

candidates.rationale: Requiring MFA for unprivileged system users may prevent abuse of Valid Accounts (T1078) when an adversary has obtained a password but cannot satisfy the additional factor.

evidence.statement: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate unprivileged human users of systems.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends MFA across account types to reduce abuse of compromised valid credentials.

candidates.rationale: Requiring MFA for privileged system users may prevent privileged Valid Accounts (T1078) from being abused with a compromised password alone.

evidence.statement: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate privileged human users of systems.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends MFA across account types to reduce abuse of compromised valid credentials.

candidates.rationale: Routing administrative activity through jump servers constrains Remote Services (T1021) by limiting direct network paths to managed administrative gateways.

evidence.statement: Administrative activities are conducted through jump servers.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends gateways and similar mechanisms to limit unnecessary remote access to sensitive systems.

candidates.rationale: Blocking internet advertisements in browsers may prevent the malicious-advertising delivery path used by Drive-by Compromise (T1189).

evidence.statement: Web browsers do not process web advertisements from the internet.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK states that ad blockers can prevent malicious code served through advertisements from executing.

candidates.rationale: MFA on organisational online services processing sensitive data may prevent access through compromised Valid Accounts (T1078) when only a password is available.

evidence.statement: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate human users to their organisation’s online services that process, store or communicate their organisation’s sensitive data.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends MFA across account types to reduce abuse of compromised valid credentials.

candidates.rationale: MFA on organisational online services may prevent Brute Force (T1110) from yielding access when password guessing succeeds but the additional factor is unavailable.

evidence.statement: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate human users to their organisation’s online services that process, store or communicate their organisation’s sensitive data.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends MFA, including on externally facing services, as a mitigation for brute force.

candidates.rationale: Performing and retaining business-aligned backups supports recovery after Data Encrypted for Impact (T1486) by preserving restorable copies.

evidence.statement: Backups of data, applications and settings are performed and retained in accordance with business criticality and business continuity requirements.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends regular, tested, protected backups to restore data after encryption for impact.

candidates.rationale: PowerShell Constrained Language Mode constrains PowerShell (T1059.001) by restricting dangerous language elements and arbitrary Windows API access.

evidence.statement: PowerShell is configured to use Constrained Language Mode.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK specifically identifies PowerShell Constrained Language Mode as restricting dangerous PowerShell language elements.

candidates.rationale: Restricting executables and scripts to an approved set may prevent a Malicious File (T1204.002) from running after user execution.

evidence.statement: Application control restricts the execution of executables, libraries, scripts, installers, compiled HTML, HTML applications and control panel applets to an organisation-approved set.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK states application control may prevent executables masquerading as other files from running.

candidates.rationale: Enabling antivirus scanning for Office macros may prevent malicious Visual Basic (T1059.005) macro code by detecting and quarantining the containing file.

evidence.statement: Microsoft Office macro antivirus scanning is enabled.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK states antivirus can automatically quarantine suspicious files used for Visual Basic execution.

candidates.rationale: Credential Guard constrains LSASS Memory (T1003.001) credential dumping by isolating LSA secrets, although ATT&CK notes it does not stop every dumping method.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK identifies Credential Guard as protecting LSA secrets while noting incomplete coverage of credential dumping.

candidates.rationale: Applying vendor fixes to online services within the stated window may prevent Exploit Public-Facing Application (T1190) against vulnerabilities covered by those fixes.

evidence.statement: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in online services are applied within two weeks of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends patch management for externally exposed applications.

candidates.rationale: Patching workstation, internal-server, and network-device operating systems may prevent Exploitation of Remote Services (T1210) where the exploited flaw is covered by the update.

evidence.statement: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of workstations, non-internet-facing servers and non-internet-facing network devices are applied within one month of release.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends patch management for internal enterprise endpoints and servers.

candidates.rationale: Preventing ordinary privileged accounts from modifying or deleting backups constrains Data Destruction (T1485) by preserving recovery copies outside those accounts’ reach.

evidence.statement: Privileged user accounts (excluding backup administrator accounts) are prevented from modifying and deleting backups.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends off-system backups protected from adversary access and destruction.

candidates.rationale: Secure and resilient retention of backups supports recovery after Data Destruction (T1485) by preserving organisational data outside the destructive event.

evidence.statement: Backups of data, applications and settings are retained in a secure and resilient manner.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends off-system backups protected from adversary access and destruction.

candidates.rationale: Enabling Local Security Authority protection constrains LSASS Memory (T1003.001) dumping by running LSA as a protected process.

evidence.statement: Local Security Authority protection functionality is enabled.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends enabling Protected Process Light for LSA against LSASS memory credential dumping.
